titleEn: This Is What a Big Brother Does!

pages.text: "Mom, look at me!" Quick-handed monkey Taro bounced on the porch. Mom held and patted his baby sibling, wrapped in leaves. She put a finger to her lips. Outside, rain fell.
"Beside Mom is my place!" Taro pouted. A baby filled her lap, and leaves for the baby's bed filled the space beside her. There was nowhere for Taro to sit.
Taro went to the porch's edge and sat with his back turned. Water dripped from the eaves. Inside, only the baby's laughter rang out.
Mom called, "There's an empty place here." Taro slowly looked back. Mom patted the space beside her.
Taro sat beside the baby. The little face frowned and fussed. "What's wrong?" Taro looked carefully. The baby's hands kept grasping at the air.
Taro took a branch and tapped the porch softly twice. The baby stopped crying and smiled, gripping his finger tightly with a little hand.
"Mom! I made the baby stop crying!" Taro lifted his shoulders proudly. "This Is What a Big Brother Does!" The baby would not let go of his finger.
The rain stopped. Taro waved a leaf, playing peekaboo. The baby kicked little feet, eyes following only Taro. Meanwhile, Mom tidied the porch.

There were three big-brother rules: one, when the baby cries, see what's needed! Two, make soft sounds! Three, stay beside the baby when Mom's hands are busy! Taro stayed beside the baby when the evening lamp was lit, too.

Mom hugged Taro and the baby together. A new sibling did not mean his place was gone; it gave a big brother's hands something to do. "Mom, I'll help the baby stop crying tomorrow, too! This Is What a Big Brother Does!"
